paragraphs.source_en:
55 Under the bowers
Where the Ocean Powers
Sit on their pearlèd thrones,
Through the coral woods
Of the weltering floods,
60 Over heaps of unvalued stones;
Through the dim beams,
Which amid the streams
Weave a network of coloured light,
And under the caves,
65 Where the shadowy waves
Are as green as the forest’s night: —
Outspeeding the shark,
And the swordfish dark,
Under the Ocean foam,
70 And up through the rifts
Of the mountain clifts,
They passed to their Dorian home,

paragraphs.source_en:
And now from their fountains
In Enna’s Mountains,
75 Down one vale where the morning basks,
Like friends once parted,
Grown single hearted,
They ply their watery tasks.
 At sunrise they leap
80 From their cradles steep
In the cave of the shelving hill;
At noon-tide they flow
Through the woods below
And the meadows of Asphodel, —

paragraphs.source_en:
Of the swinging floods Nbk 14. weltering floods] Rolling waves.
 unvalued] Invaluable (OED 1). Cp. PU IV 281 and n.
 the forest’s] a forests Nbk 14.
 swordfish] xiphias Nbk 14; the classical name for the swordfish.
 Ocean foam] Nbk 14, 1824. Koszul notes that Mary’s fair copy reads ‘Ocean’ foam as if a genitive was
meant; but cf. Ocean foam in the Song of Apollo [line 9]’, written shortly after for Midas, Mary’s other
mythological drama.
 clifts] Cliffs (OED n2). Cp. May-day Night (Longman vi, no. 440) ii 47.
 their Dorian home] S. identifies Sicily as a Greek (Dorian) outpost.
 Enna’s Mountains] Enna is a raised plateau in central Sicily from which, according to Greek myth,
Proserpine was abducted by Pluto. S. relocates the sources of Alpheus and Arethusa from Greece to
Sicily.
 Like friends . . . hearted] Cp. These are two friends whose lives were undivided (Longman iv
